about: The website-business playbook (Agency > Expert, team web-expert 2026-11-20): how to position, price, pitch, build and keep local-business website clients, 3D / immersive sites included. One file: agency/expert/ draws it and Jarvis answers from it (jarvis/biz.js 'web'). Offline, no AI service.
honest: Prices are typical ranges for a solo studio selling to US local businesses in 2026, not quotes and not promises. Never invent clients, reviews or results; say it is a sales call; stop when asked.

offers.name: Starter site
offers.what: 5 pages, mobile first, click-to-call, Google Business Profile linked, contact form, basic local SEO (titles, schema, map).

offers.name: Growth site
offers.what: Starter + 10-15 pages (one per service and town), reviews widget, booking or quote form, speed under 2 s on a phone, analytics with a monthly one-page report.

offers.name: 3D / immersive site
offers.what: Growth site + one 3D piece that sells: a walk-through of the space, a product you can spin, or a scroll story. Built light (loads in under 3 s on a phone), with a plain fallback.

offers.name: Care plan (retainer)
offers.what: Hosting, updates, backups, 2 small changes a month, a monthly report with calls and form leads.

offers.name: Local growth plan (retainer)
offers.what: Care plan + Google Business Profile posts weekly, review requests, 2 new pages a month, rank tracking for 10 town + service searches.

offers.name: Google Business Profile fix
offers.what: Claim / verify, categories, services, 20 photos, Q&A, review link and a review-request card. The fastest win for most trades.

offers.name: Small-budget ads
offers.what: Google Local Services Ads or Search ads on a $500-$1,500 a month budget (paid to Google by the client), set up + managed.

niches.name: Roofer
niches.pain: Leads come from Google and storms; a weak site loses the quote to the roofer with photos and reviews.
niches.hook: Before / after photo galleries by town and a 60-second instant-estimate form.
niches.say: Most homeowners pick the roofer whose site shows real roofs in their own town. Yours shows [what they show]. I built a preview with a before / after gallery and an instant-estimate form: can I send you the link?

niches.name: Plumber / HVAC
niches.pain: Emergency calls: speed and trust win; most calls come from Google Maps on a phone.
niches.hook: Click-to-call at the top, service-area pages, 24/7 badge, reviews.
niches.say: When a pipe bursts, people call the first plumber whose site loads fast and shows a phone number. Yours takes [x] seconds on a phone. I made a preview that loads in under 2: want the link?

niches.name: Landscaper / pool builder
niches.pain: Big-ticket outdoor projects sold on looks; clients cannot picture the result.
niches.hook: A 3D yard you can turn, or a scroll story of one finished project.
niches.say: Your work is visual and your clients spend [x] on a project they cannot picture yet. A 3D walk-through of one of your finished yards lets them see it on their phone. I made a quick preview: can I show you?

niches.name: Home builder / remodeler
niches.pain: Six-figure jobs; buyers compare portfolios for weeks.
niches.hook: 3D walk-throughs of past builds and floor plans you can tap.
niches.say: People spend weeks choosing a builder and compare portfolios at night on their phones. A walk-through of your best build keeps them on your site instead of the next builder's. I made a preview of one: may I send it?

niches.name: Dentist / med spa
niches.pain: New-patient bookings online; trust, prices and the office matter.
niches.hook: Online booking, treatment pages with prices from, a calm tour of the office.
niches.say: New patients now book online at 10 pm. Your site sends them to a phone line that is closed. I made a preview with booking on every page: can I send you the link?

niches.name: Restaurant / cafe
niches.pain: Menu, hours and ordering on a phone; Google Maps is the real front door.
niches.hook: A fast menu page, online ordering link, the Google profile fixed.
niches.say: Most of your guests see your Google listing before your website. Yours is missing [photos / hours / menu]. I can fix the listing this week for a flat fee: want me to show you what is missing?

niches.name: Wedding / event venue
niches.pain: Couples book after a tour; out-of-town couples cannot visit first.
niches.hook: A 3D tour of the space, set up for a ceremony and a reception.
niches.say: Couples who cannot visit still book from a tour. A 3D walk-through of your hall set for a wedding lets them stand in it from their sofa. I made a short preview: can I send it?

niches.name: Real estate agent / property
niches.pain: Listings and the agent's own brand; buyers expect tours.
niches.hook: Listing pages with 3D tours and a neighbourhood guide that ranks.
niches.say: Buyers expect to walk through a home online first. Your own site sends them to the portal, where the next agent is one tap away. I made a preview with a tour on your page: want to see it?

niches.name: Car dealer / auto shop
niches.pain: Dealers: inventory and trust; shops: reviews and quick quotes.
niches.hook: Dealers: a car you can spin; shops: an instant-quote form and reviews.
niches.say: Your customers compare three shops on their phone before they call. I made a preview that shows your reviews and a quote form at the top: can I send it?

niches.name: Furniture / product maker
niches.pain: Buyers want to see size, finish and how it looks in a room.
niches.hook: A product you can spin and zoom, in 3 finishes.
niches.say: People buying a [table] want to turn it and see the grain. A 3D view of one of your pieces does that on a phone. I made a quick one: can I show you?

niches.name: Gym / studio
niches.pain: Trial sign-ups and the schedule on a phone.
niches.hook: A free-trial form at the top, the class schedule, a short tour.
niches.say: People decide on a gym in two minutes on their phone. Yours makes them hunt for the schedule and the price. I made a preview with a free-trial button at the top: want the link?

niches.name: Lawyer / accountant
niches.pain: Trust and clarity; 3D would look unserious.
niches.hook: Clear practice pages, a consultation form, reviews and credentials.
niches.say: People hire a [lawyer] they trust in the first 10 seconds. Your site leads with [x]. I made a calmer preview that leads with what you do and a consultation form: can I send it?

cards.title: Positioning: who you are for
say: I build websites that get local [trade] businesses more calls from Google.
I work with [trade] in [area] only, so I know what your customers search for.
do: Pick 1-2 trades and one area; say it in every call and on your own site.
Show one real preview per trade before you have clients: a preview is honest, a fake client is not.
cards.usd: A niche lets you charge the top of each range: buyers pay more for someone who knows their trade.
cards.avoid: Saying you do every kind of website for everyone.

cards.title: Pricing: three options, middle first
say: Most [trade] businesses pick the middle one: [Growth] at [$4,500], ready in 3 weeks.
The first one gets you online; the third one is for when the site itself has to sell the job.
do: Always show 3 options: Starter $1,500-$3,000, Growth $3,500-$6,500, 3D / immersive $6,000-$15,000.
Add a care plan ($99-$299 a month) to every site: it is the income that stays.
Take 50% up front, 50% at launch.
cards.usd: A solo studio doing 2 Growth sites + 6 care plans a month: about $9,000 + $1,200 a month recurring.
cards.avoid: Hourly prices, or one price with no choice (the client then compares you to cheap builders).

cards.title: Pricing a 3D / immersive site
say: The 3D piece is priced on what it sells: if one extra [wedding / build] a year comes from it, it paid for itself.
It starts at [$6,000] with the full site; the 3D part alone is [$2,500-$6,000].
do: Price 3D as an add-on to a Growth site: +$2,500 (a product you can spin) to +$6,000 (a walk-through of a space).
Quote a fixed number of rooms / products; extra ones $400-$900 each.
Always ship a plain fallback and keep the first load under 3 s on a phone.
cards.usd: 3D / immersive: $6,000-$15,000 total; add-on $2,500-$6,000; extra rooms or products $400-$900 each.
cards.avoid: 3D for trades sold on speed (plumbers, HVAC, lawyers): it slows the site and looks like a gimmick.

cards.title: 3D: when it sells, when it is a gimmick
say: 3D is worth it when the customer is buying the place or the object: a venue, a home, a yard, a piece of furniture.
For an emergency trade I would not do 3D: speed and reviews win that call.
do: Sells: venues, real estate, home builders, landscapers / pools, furniture and product makers, showrooms.
Maybe: dentists / med spas (a calm office tour), gyms, car dealers (a car you can spin).
Gimmick: plumbers, HVAC, lawyers, accountants, restaurants (fix the Google listing instead).
cards.usd: Only pitch 3D where one extra sale pays for it ($6,000+ jobs).
cards.avoid: Heavy 3D on the home page with no fallback: a slow phone means a lost lead.

cards.title: Cold outreach: the 30-second opener
say: Hi, is this the owner of [Business]? This is [me] with [my studio], it is a sales call so I will be quick: I made a free preview of a new site for [Business]. Can I take 30 seconds to tell you why?
Thanks. I called because [one real issue: no site / slow on phones / no reviews shown]. The preview fixes that.
do: Call 10:00-11:30 or 14:00-16:00 local time, never during their rush.
Make the preview before the call (Agency > Demos).
One goal per call: permission to send the link.
cards.usd: Typical: 1 meeting per 15-25 calls, 1 sale per 4-6 meetings: about 100 calls for one $3,500 site.
cards.avoid: Calling numbers on the Do Not Call list with a pre-recorded message, or pretending to be a customer.

cards.title: Objection answers
say: 'We get enough work.' - Great; then the site is about better jobs, not more: the preview shows your biggest projects first.
'Too expensive.' - The Starter is [$1,500]: one job pays for it. Which of the three is closest?
'My nephew does our site.' - Keep him; I can just fix the Google listing, that is where most calls come from.
'Send me an email.' - Happy to; the preview link is in it. What is the best address?
'Not interested.' - Understood, I will not call again. Have a good day.
do: Answer, then ask one small question; never argue twice.
'Not interested' ends the call and goes on the do-not-call list.
cards.avoid: Pressure, fake deadlines, made-up competitor stories.

cards.title: Local SEO: what actually moves calls
say: People search '[service] near me' or '[service] [town]'. You need one page for each service and each town you serve.
do: One page per service + town (e.g. 'Roof repair in [Town]'), with real photos.
Name, address, phone the same everywhere (site, Google, Yelp, Facebook).
LocalBusiness schema, a fast phone page, the map embedded.
cards.usd: Local growth plan: $400-$1,200 a month; first results in 2-4 months.

cards.title: Google Business Profile: the fastest win
say: Most of your calls start on your Google listing, not your website. Yours is missing [photos / services / hours]. I can fix it this week for a flat [$450].
do: Right primary category, all services, 20+ real photos, weekly posts, Q&A answered.
A review link + a small card to hand to every happy customer.
cards.usd: $300-$750 one time; often the first sale that leads to the site.
cards.avoid: Fake reviews or review gating: against Google's rules and the FTC's.

cards.title: Reviews: the engine
say: Ask every happy customer the same day: 'Would you leave us a quick Google review? Here is the link.'
do: A text with the review link after each job (the client sends it).
Show the newest reviews on the site's first screen.
Reply to every review within 2 days, the bad ones politely.
cards.usd: Part of the Local growth plan; going from 10 to 50 reviews is often the biggest lift in calls.
cards.avoid: Paying for reviews or only asking happy customers through a filter.

cards.title: Conversion: turning visits into calls
say: Your site gets visits; it needs to turn more of them into calls. The top of the page should say what you do, where, and show the phone number.
do: Phone + a short form above the fold on a phone.
One clear button per page ('Get a free estimate').
Loads in under 2 s on a phone; real photos; reviews near the button.
cards.usd: A redesign that doubles the contact rate is worth more to a client than more traffic.
cards.avoid: Sliders, auto-playing video and pop-ups on the first screen.

cards.title: Ads on a small budget
say: For [trade], Google's Local Services Ads charge per lead, not per click: start with $500 a month and see the cost per call.
do: Trades: Local Services Ads first (Google Guaranteed); then Search ads on 5-10 exact local searches.
Send ads to a page made for that service, not the home page.
Report cost per call every month.
cards.usd: Client budget $500-$1,500 a month (paid to Google); your management $250-$600 a month.
cards.avoid: Broad keywords, sending ads to the home page, no call tracking.

cards.title: Retainers: the income that stays
say: After launch, I keep the site fast, safe and updated, and send you a one-page report every month: [$149] a month.
do: Every site comes with a care plan; offer the Local growth plan after 60 days with the first report.
Month-to-month, cancel anytime: it sells better than a contract.
cards.usd: 20 care plans at $149 = about $3,000 a month before you build anything new.
cards.avoid: Free hosting 'for now': it is hard to start charging later.

cards.title: Upsells that make sense
say: Your best page now is [service]. A page for each town you serve would bring that search in [Town] too.
do: Town + service pages ($150-$300 each).
Booking or quote calculator ($500-$1,500).
A 3D piece for one product or space ($2,500+), only where it sells.
Photography day ($400-$900) when the photos are weak.
cards.usd: Upsells usually add 30-60% to a client's first-year value.
cards.avoid: Upselling before the first report shows results.

cards.title: Build process: 3 weeks, no surprises
say: Week 1 you see the design, week 2 the full site, week 3 we launch. Two rounds of changes are included.
do: Kick-off call: services, towns, photos, reviews, competitors.
Design on a phone first; launch only after a phone speed check.
Hand over: logins, a 1-page guide, the first report date.
cards.usd: Deposit 50%, balance at launch; changes after 2 rounds $95 an hour.
cards.avoid: Starting without the deposit or without the client's photos and logins.

options: Old or slow on a phone

options: Yes: the place or the object sells
